extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO patent examiners
extracted.subtask_short: US patent application filing and drafting
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/formatting requirements for filing and drafting U.S. patent applications (specification, claims, papers, electronic media) and related fee/refund procedures under the MPEP and applicable CFR/ statutes. Covers disclosure/substance (35 U.S.C. 112), paper/electronic form (37 C.F.R. 1.52, 1.96, 1.821), fee application and refund rules (37 C.F.R. 1.16, 1.26, 1.28), and compact-disc/electronic submission specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of restriction on nonelected claims for fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: After a requirement for restriction, nonelected claims will be included in determining the fees due in connection with a subsequent amendment unless such claims are canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment canceling claims accompanying the papers constituting the application will be effective to diminish the number of claims to be considered in calculating the filing fees to be paid. A preliminary amendment filed concurrently with a response to a Notice To File Missing Parts of Application that cancels or adds claims will be taken into account in determining the appropriate fees due in response to the Notice. No refund will be made for claims being canceled in the response that have already been paid for. Money paid in connection with the filing of a proposed amendment will not be refunded by reason of the nonentry of the amendment; unentered claims will not be counted when calculating the fee due in subsequent amendments. Amendments affecting the claims cannot serve as the basis for granting any refund (see MPEP § 607.02 V for refund of excess claims fees). Excess claims fees set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) apply to excess claims presented during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-electronic filing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional fee applies for non-electronic filing of certain original patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 10(h) of Public Law 112-29 provides that an additional fee of $400 ($200 for a small entity) shall be established for each application for an original (i.e., non-reissue) patent, except for a design, plant, or provisional application, not filed by electronic means. See 37 CFR 1.16(t) for the non-electronic fee applicable to applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) filed on or after November 15, 2011 other than by the USPTO’s electronic filing system (EFS-Web).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of applying insufficient payment — nonprovisional under 35 U.S.C. 111(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a payment submitted on filing is insufficient and the applicant has not specified how to apply it, the Office will apply the payment in a prescribed order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will apply the payment in the following order until the payment is expended: (1) basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(a),(b),(c), or (e)); (2) non-electronic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(t)); (3) application size fee (37 CFR 1.16(s)); (4) late filing surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(f)); (5) processing fee for non-English application (37 CFR 1.17(i)); (6) search fee (37 CFR 1.16(k),(l),(m), or (n)); (7) examination fee (37 CFR 1.16(o),(p),(q), or (r)); and (8) excess claims fee (37 CFR 1.16(h),(i), and (j)). See also MPEP § 509.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of applying insufficient payment — provisional under 35 U.S.C. 111(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional application payment is insufficient and the applicant has not specified application of payment, the Office will apply it in a prescribed order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will apply payment in the following order until expended: (1) basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(d)); (2) application size fee (37 CFR 1.16(s)); and (3) late filing surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(g)). See also MPEP § 509.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of deposit account authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: How the Office treats deposit account authorizations to charge various fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A deposit account authorization to charge “the filing fee” is treated as an authorization to charge the applicable fees under 37 CFR 1.16 (the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, any excess claims fee, and any application size fee) to the deposit account. An authorization to charge “the basic filing fee” is treated as an authorization to charge the applicable basic filing fee, search fee, and examination fee. Any deposit account authorization to charge the filing fee but not the search fee or examination fee must specifically limit the authorization by reference to one or more of paragraphs (a) through (e) of 37 CFR 1.16. The Office treats such authorizations as received on the date of receipt as defined in 37 CFR 1.6 for refund purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund eligibility — general rule (37 CFR 1.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may refund any fee paid by mistake or any amount paid in excess of that required; change of purpose after payment does not entitle refund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.26(a): The Director may refund any fee paid by mistake or in excess. A change of purpose after payment of a fee (e.g., withdrawing a filing) will not entitle a party to a refund. The Office will not refund amounts of $25 or less unless a refund is specifically requested and will not notify the payor of such amounts. Requests for refund must generally be filed within two years from the date the fee was paid (37 CFR 1.26(b)), except as otherwise provided. If banking information is not provided, the Office may require it or use banking info on the payment instrument to make refund. Credit card refunds will be credited to the charged credit card account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund timelines and special deposit-account timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Time periods and special rules for requesting refunds involving deposit account charges and exceptions are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request for refund must be filed within two years from the date the fee was paid; if the Office charges a deposit account by an amount other than specifically indicated, refund requests based on such charge must be filed within two years from the date of the deposit account statement indicating such charge and must include a copy of that statement. The two-year periods are not extendable. For deposit-account charge authorizations, the refund period begins on the date the charge authorization is received in the Office (with specific rules for 37 CFR 1.8 certificates and Priority Mail Express®).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds for reexamination or supplemental examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director decides not to institute reexamination (ex parte or inter partes) or supplemental examination, specified refunds will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For an ex parte reexamination request, the ex parte reexamination filing fee paid by the requester, less the fee set forth in § 1.20(c)(7), will be refunded if the Director decides not to institute. For an inter partes reexamination request, a refund of $7,970 will be made to the requester if the Director decides not to institute. For a supplemental examination request, the fee for reexamination ordered as a result of supplemental examination (§ 1.20(k)(2)) will be returned to the patent owner who requested the supplemental examination if the Director decides not to institute. Refunds will generally be issued in the form that the original payment was provided; the requester should indicate the form for refund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited refundability of certain fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain fees are not refundable except if paid by mistake or in excess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basic filing fee, non-electronic filing fee, the examination fee, and the application size fee cannot be refunded unless the fee was paid by mistake or in excess of that required. The Office may refund the search fee and any excess claims fee if applicant files a petition under 37 CFR 1.138(d) to expressly abandon the application before an examination has been made (see MPEP § 711.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirement under 35 U.S.C. 112(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a valid patent, the application as filed must contain a full and clear disclosure of the invention in the manner prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement ensures the public receives something in return for exclusionary rights. All amendments and claims must find descriptive basis in the original disclosure; no new matter may be introduced after filing. Applicant may rely on the specification with original claims and drawings as filed. Examiners should object to language deemed offensive under 37 CFR 1.3 for lack of decorum and courtesy; offensive depictions or caricatures in drawings should similarly be objected to. See MPEP § 714.25 for amendments and papers presented in violation of 37 CFR 1.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification written-description and enablement requirements (37 CFR 1.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must include a written description of the invention and of the manner and process of making and using the same, in full, clear, concise, and exact terms to enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification must set forth the precise invention in a manner to distinguish it from what is old, describe a specific embodiment, explain mode of operation when applicable, and set forth the best mode contemplated by the inventor. For improvements, the specification must point out the part(s) to which the improvement relates and confine description to the specific improvement and cooperating parts as necessary. The specification is a written description and must not include information unrelated to applicant's invention; examiners should object and require correction where such unrelated info appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and related parts must commence on separate pages
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification, claims, abstract, and sequence listing (if any) must each begin on separate physical sheets/pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification must commence on a separate sheet; each sheet including part of the specification may not include other parts of the application. The claim(s), abstract and sequence listing should not be included on a sheet including any other part of the application. The claim(s) must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page (§ 1.75(h)). The abstract must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page or be submitted as the first page of the patent in a reissue application or reexamination or supplemental examination proceeding (§ 1.72(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification formality and minor informalities (form paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should use standard form paragraphs to point out minor informalities or more severe defects in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.29 used for minor informalities (e.g., spelling errors, inconsistent terminology). Form paragraphs 6.29–6.31 address spacing of lines, numerous errors requiring revision to comply with 35 U.S.C. 112(a), and lengthy specifications that should be checked and corrected. Examiners should require revisions where a newly filed application obviously fails to disclose with the clarity required by 35 U.S.C. 112.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper physical requirements (37 CFR 1.52(a),(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical papers to become part of the USPTO record must meet paper size, margin, orientation, printing, and legibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers must be on sheets of the same size, not permanently bound, with top margin at least 2.0 cm (3/4 inch), left margin at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), bottom margin at least 2.0 cm, written only on one side in portrait orientation, plainly and legibly written by typewriter or machine printer in permanent dark ink or equivalent, and have sufficient clarity/contrast for direct reproduction by photographic, electrostatic, photo-offset, microfilming, and electronic capture. Papers should have no holes. The provisions do not apply to pre-printed Office forms or to certain double-column formats in reissue/reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification text formatting (spacing, font, columns, page/paragraph numbering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications (other than reissue and certain proceedings) must meet spacing, paper-size, font, column, and numbering requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification should be on flexible, strong, smooth, non-shiny, durable, white paper; lines 1 1/2 or double spaced; paper either DIN A4 or 8.5x11 inches with specified margins; text in nonscript type font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, Courier), preferably font size 12, capitals at least 0.3175 cm high, but may be no smaller than 0.21 cm (font size 6); only a single column of text. Pages of specification (including claims and abstract) must be numbered consecutively starting with 1, centered above or preferably below the text. Paragraphs (other than claims/abstract) may be numbered using Arabic numerals in square brackets (e.g., [0001]) with leading zeros, highlighted in bold, and treated consistently with nontext elements being part of the surrounding paragraph. Paragraph/section headers are not paragraphs and should not be numbered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlineation, erasure, cancellation and substitute specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Alterations to application papers and the conditions under which a substitute specification may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlineation, erasure, cancellation, or other alteration of application papers may be made before or after signing the inventor's oath/declaration provided the statements in the oath/declaration remain applicable. A substitute specification (§ 1.125) may be required if the application papers do not comply with 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirements for non-English filings (37 CFR 1.52(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional and provisional applications may be filed in a language other than English, but specific translation and processing fee requirements apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is filed in a non-English language, an English translation, a statement the translation is accurate, and the processing fee (§ 1.17(i)) are required; if not filed, applicant will be notified and given time to file to avoid abandonment. A provisional application filed in a non-English language does not require an English translation at the provisional stage; see § 1.78(a) for claiming benefit in a later nonprovisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic documents and compact disc submission rules (37 CFR 1.52(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific categories of documents may be submitted on compact disc and must conform to format, labeling, and transmittal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed on compact disc: computer program listings (§ 1.96), Sequence Listings (§ 1.821(c)), and large tables. Each CD must conform to ISO 9660 and contain ASCII content. CDs must be enclosed in a hard case within an unsealed padded envelope and accompanied by a transmittal letter listing machine format, operating system compatibility, files, sizes, dates, and other info. CDs will not be returned. Duplicate CDs required unless only a Sequence Listing; replacements must be labeled as replacements and accompanied by a statement that the replacement contains no new matter. The specification must contain an incorporation-by-reference paragraph identifying each CD's files, dates, and sizes; the Office may require paper inclusion of parts previously submitted on CD. CDs must be labeled with inventor names, title, docket/application number, creation date, order if multiple, and indication of Copy 1/Copy 2. Unreadable files on both copies will be treated as not having been submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee counting rules for electronic materials
rubrics_metrics.description: How electronic submissions and specific listings are counted for the application size fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any sequence listing in compliance with §§ 1.52(e) and 1.821(c) and any computer program listing filed in an electronic medium in compliance with §§ 1.52(e) and 1.96 will be excluded when determining the application size fee required by § 1.16(s) or § 1.492(j). For applications with specification and drawings submitted on an electronic medium other than EFS, each three kilobytes of content submitted on an electronic medium shall be counted as a sheet of paper for fee determination. For submissions via the Office electronic filing system, the paper size equivalent will be considered 75% of the number of sheets when rendered by the Office electronic filing system; sequence listings and computer program listings submitted via EFS in ASCII text as part of associated files will be excluded when determining application size fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical and mathematical formulae and tables rules (37 CFR 1.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on inclusion of chemical/mathematical formulae, tables, and their placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification may contain chemical and mathematical formulae but shall not contain drawings or flow diagrams. The description portion may contain tables, but the same tables should not be included in both the drawings and description portions. Claims may contain tables if necessary to conform to 35 U.S.C. 112 or otherwise desirable. Tables submitted in electronic form must comply with § 1.58(c) and related provisions.
